citation: Rosa, Rui, Katja Trübenbach, Marta S. Pimentel, Joana Boavida-Portugal, Filipa Faleiro, Miguel Baptista, Gisela Dionísio, Ricardo Calado, Hans O. Pörtner, and Tiago Repolho. "Differential impacts of ocean acidification and warming on winter and summer progeny of a coastal squid (Loligo vulgaris)." Journal of Experimental Biology 217, no. 4 (2014): 518-525.
minor_concerns: Eggs were collected from the wild.
notes_moderators: Data for parlarvae from eggs collected in Winter. The LT50 was measured while the temperature was increased gradually; and the percentage of living animals at each temperature was determined. This is an hybrid between CTmax and LT50, hence why a ramping rate was assigned but not n_test_temp. Set_time was taken as 30 min because temperatures was increased every 30 min and the survival of the animals was assessed before each ramp. salinity, pH, acc_temp_var and acclimation temperatures were averaged between treatments (see table S3 for original values). n_test_temp was taken as 20 because temperature was increased at a rate of 1C/30min from the temperature of acclimation until all animals died and 20 * 3 animals were used for each treatment. Assuming a maximum temperature reached of 39C (which seems consistent with LT100 values displayed in Fig. 5), we can asssume n_test_temp to be approximatively 20.
notes_es: Data digitised from figure. Sample sizes were taken as the number of test temperatures * the number of replicate test temperatures. Note that n_test_temp was estimated and is not exact. Although authors report "standard deviations", these values seem closer to standard errors (and estimations from linear regressions usually return standard errors) so we considered the sd_low and sd_high as SE instead of SD.
